title: Constituent Assembly election
summary: The election of 25 April 1975, held on the first anniversary of the coup, was the first in Portugal with universal adult suffrage and the first free election since the 1920s; turnout was over ninety per cent. It chose the assembly that wrote the 1976 constitution, and the parties had signed a pact with the Armed Forces Movement beforehand that fixed the military's place in the new institutions whatever the result. The Socialists took about thirty-eight per cent and the Popular Democrats about twenty-six, against about twelve and a half for the Communists, a result far from the direction the provisional government was then taking. The distance between the vote and the government's course is the substance of the "hot summer" that followed it. It is in the atlas as the first measurement of what the country actually wanted, and as evidence in every later argument about 1975.
